sectors.name: Technology
themes: US hyperscaler AI capex and cloud demand continue to re-rate global tech multiples, lifting Indonesian-listed tech proxies via sentiment and foreign flows.
Indonesia's digital economy—e-commerce, fintech, and logistics—is consolidating around profitable leaders, with local players like DIVA and PGJO gaining share amid regulatory tightening.
Semiconductor and hardware supply chain resilience (MPWR, COHR, 2454) supports premium valuations, but Indonesia's tech index remains hostage to IDR volatility and domestic rate expectations.
sectors.ai: Buy selective large-cap tech with US cloud/AI exposure (AMZN, GOOGL, MPWR) and Indonesian digital enablers (DIVA, PGJO) on earnings momentum; trim pure-ID laggards until rupiah stabilizes. Position for Q3 AI capex cycle and local e-commerce consolidation, targeting 8-12% upside over 4-6 weeks.

sectors.name: Financials

Specialty insurers (ERIE, LPGI) are capitalizing on hard-market premium rates and disciplined underwriting, sustaining margin expansion into 2025.
Indonesian financials remain pressured by weak loan growth and high funding costs, but digital banking adoption and infrastructure financing offer long-term structural upside.
sectors.ai: Rotate into US alternative asset managers (ARES, APO) and specialty insurers (ERIE, LPGI) on durable fee-related earnings and hard-market pricing; trim Indonesian laggards (TIFA, TRIM) as domestic liquidity stays thin. Favor US over ID for near-term alpha, but keep ID exposure for long-term structural growth.

The widening IDX vs US performance gap signals capital rotation into Indonesian consumer equities, favoring smaller caps with high beta to local demand cycles over multinational peers.
sectors.ai: Buy selective consumer names on IDX strength, led by IATA and ERTX, as domestic demand resilience outpaces US weakness; rotate into high-momentum FMCG plays with local earnings catalysts, but trim exposure if IDX aggregate momentum fades below +0.2%.

sectors.name: Infrastructure
themes: Government's accelerated infrastructure spending under the new cabinet's fiscal expansion is a durable driver, favoring contractors like JKON and gas utilities like RGAS with direct project pipelines.

Rupiah stability and falling US rate expectations improve financing conditions for leveraged infrastructure firms, making TKIM and MIRA more attractive as cost-of-capital tailwinds persist.

Rotate into ETN and TKIM for export-linked logistics exposure, but avoid chasing LMAX/VRT without volume confirmation. Hold MIRA as a laggard catch-up play. Position for Q3 capex announcements and Jokowi legacy projects; trim any position that breaks its 20-day moving average.

sectors.name: Healthcare
themes: Indonesia's hospital bed expansion and JKN coverage growth are structurally lifting local operators like SILO and MTMH, independent of US biotech sentiment.

US pharma pricing reform and R&D productivity divergence favor large-cap innovators (REGN, MERK) but reward selective exposure, not broad sector beta, in a normal-signal tape.
sectors.ai: Buy healthcare selectively: DXCM's +11.95% confirms CGM demand resilience, while SILO, WIRG, and MTMH show Indonesia's local hospital/pharma names are decoupling from US weakness. Rotate into domestic operators (SILO, MTMH) and US device leaders (DXCM) over REITs; avoid laggards like REGN despite its bounce. Signal NORMAL allows adding on dips, but keep beta low—target 5% overweight in hospitals and diagnostics.
